questions.title: Least-squares inference for a stationary zero-mean AR(1)
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation in time-series statistics. Let X_t=phi X_{t-1}+epsilon_t for t=1,...,T, with |phi|<1, a stationary zero-mean initialization, and iid innovations independent of the past with mean zero, variance sigma_epsilon^2>0, and enough moments for the law of large numbers and martingale central limit theorem. For the no-intercept least-squares estimator phi_hat=[sum_{t=1}^T X_{t-1}X_t]/[sum_{t=1}^T X_{t-1}^2], develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of the exact error decomposition, the stationary variance gamma_0=sigma_epsilon^2/(1-phi^2), consistency, and sqrt(T)(phi_hat-phi) converging in distribution to N(0,1-phi^2). State why the numerator is a martingale sum, identify its limiting quadratic variance, justify the denominator limit, use Slutsky explicitly, and do not claim finite-sample unbiasedness or use simulation as proof. The required model-authored artifact is est_ar1_zero_mean_ols and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory computation may diagnose implementation or finite-sample behavior. A separate frozen confirmatory assessment uses independently generated stationary Gaussian AR(1) paths at predeclared negative, moderate, and persistent coefficients to test the exact estimator identity and the standardized asymptotic error with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: series
request_fields.meaning: One finite real-valued time-series path in chronological order, containing X_0 through X_T.
request_fields.shape: length T+1 with T>=2 and sum_{t=1}^T X_{t-1}^2>0
request_fields.units: one common measurement unit for every observation
request_fields.indexing: zero-based element j is X_j; adjacent pair (series[t-1], series[t]) represents transition t for t=1,...,T
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, fewer than three observations, and a zero lag-square denominator.

response_fields.name: n_transitions
response_fields.meaning: The number T of adjacent chronological transitions used by the estimator.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an integer at least two.
response_fields.normalization: No normalization; count every transition t=1,...,T exactly once.

response_fields.name: lag_cross_sum
response_fields.meaning: The chronological lag-one cross-product sum from X_0 X_1 through X_{T-1} X_T.
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized sum over all T adjacent transitions.

response_fields.name: lag_square_sum
response_fields.meaning: The sum of squared lagged regressors X_0 through X_{T-1}.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly positive.
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized sum over the T lagged values used as regressors.

response_fields.name: phi_hat
response_fields.meaning: The no-intercept least-squares estimate of the AR(1) coefficient for the supplied path.
response_fields.indexing: uses every transition t=1,...,T in chronological order
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite; no clipping to the stationary interval is allowed.

invariants.meaning: phi_hat equals lag_cross_sum/lag_square_sum for the exact returned sums.
Multiplying every series value by the same nonzero finite constant leaves phi_hat unchanged and multiplies both returned sums by the constant squared.

empirical_claims.meaning: The frozen confirmatory assessment compares independently generated stationary Gaussian AR(1) paths at predeclared negative, moderate, and persistent coefficients using z=sqrt(T)*(phi_hat-phi)/sqrt(1-phi^2), reports Monte Carlo uncertainty, and treats approximate centered unit-normal behavior as empirical support rather than proof.

Every confirmatory estimator call must use the exact predeclared path and contract, and the assessment separately verifies the returned finite-sample ratio identity before aggregating standardized errors.
